name: Sigma Boy
blurb: A 2024 Russian kids' pop song by Betsy and Maria Yankovskaya, a TikTok earworm
title: Sigma Boy by Betsy & Maria Yankovskaya: Why It Went Viral on TikTok
description: "Sigma Boy" is a 2024 Russian-language pop song by young singers Betsy and Maria Yankovskaya. Its catchy English hook went viral on TikTok and topped Spotify's Viral 50.
answer: "Sigma Boy" (Сигма Бой) is a dance-pop song by two Russian child singers and bloggers, Betsy and Maria Yankovskaya, released on 4 October 2024 and written by Betsy's father, composer Mikhail Chertishchev, with singer Mukka. It is sung mostly in Russian, but the repeated English hook "sigma boy" and the internet word "sigma" made it instantly memeable. TikTok creators blasting it in public and copying its chorus dance spread it worldwide in late 2024, and it briefly topped Spotify's Viral 50 Global chart.

body: Two formats drove it. One was playing the song at full volume in public, on trains or in the street, to see how strangers react, popularised by German TikTokers. The other was chorus dance videos copying the singers' simple moves. Because most listeners outside Russia cannot follow the Russian verses, the joke is that everyone still shouts the English "sigma boy" line, and the song became a favourite of Gen Alpha meme culture.

head: Date
Event
rows: Betsy and Maria Yankovskaya release "Sigma Boy" through Rhymes Music, with a simple animated audio video on YouTube.
The duo win the "Super Trend" category at a Russian children's TV channel's awards show and perform the song.
Public-speaker and dance videos spread on TikTok in Germany, South Korea and elsewhere; the song briefly tops Spotify's Viral 50 Global chart.
It reaches No. 7 on Billboard's Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart.
The YouTube upload is reported at nearly 70 million views.

body: "Sigma" is internet slang for a cool, self-confident loner, from the joke "sigma male" personality type, and by 2024 it was one of the most used Gen Alpha words. Betsy has summed up the song as: she and Maria are very cool, and the "sigma boy" is trying to win them over. The lyrics mix Russian with English words and brand names, which helped it travel.

body.note: Some listeners treat it as "brainrot" music because the lyrics sound nonsensical out of context. It is a novelty song first, not a serious statement about sigma culture.

body: A two-minute track with a chant-like English hook, a word kids already used daily, and a sound that works as a public prank or a dance clip. It charted on Spotify, YouTube, Shazam and Apple Music, and reached the singles chart in Germany. The peak was winter 2024–2025; today it is remembered as one of the defining Gen Alpha meme songs.

faq.a: Betsy and Maria Yankovskaya (also spelled Iankovskaia), two Russian child singers and bloggers. It was written by Mikhail Chertishchev and Mukka.

faq.q: What language is Sigma Boy in?
faq.a: Mostly Russian, with English words mixed in, including the title hook "sigma boy".

faq.q: Is Sigma Boy related to the sigma meme?
faq.a: Yes. The title borrows the slang word "sigma" for a cool, independent guy, which is why it spread so fast among kids who already used the word.
